title: Plastic, glass, ceramic, and wood do not let electric charge move freely
summary: Most materials are electrical insulators. Plastic, glass, ceramic, and wood hold their electrons tightly, so charge does not move freely through them.
body: OpenStax Physics says that if charge cannot move through a material, as with rubber, the material is an insulator. Most materials are insulators, because their atoms hold electrons tightly and it is hard for electrons to move from atom to atom. The insulating materials named are plastics, glass, ceramics, and wood. With enough energy, electrons can be forced through an insulator, but the insulator is often destroyed in the process. Extra charge placed on an insulator stays where it was put, instead of spreading. Semiconductors, which sit between these extremes, are a separate card.
